newsitem.title: USA: US FCC adopts rule on leased cable-TV access.
newsitem.headline: US FCC adopts rule on leased cable-TV access.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission Tuesday revised the formula cable television operators can use to charge outside parties who want to lease space on the cable system to distribute programs.
The FCC said the new formula should provide lower rates for so-called "leased access programmers."

The agency adopted an "average implicit fee" formula for calculating the maximum reasonable rate for leased access programming that is carried on a tier. This will replace the "highest implicit fee" formula which the FCC adopted in 1993.

"The commission believes that the average implicit fee is a more reasonable method for determining maximum leased access rates for tiered services because it represents the average amount non-leased access programmers effectively pay the operator for carriage," the FCC said in a release.
The National Cable Television Association, an industry trade group, gave the new formula grudging approval.

"While we believe virtually any government regulation is likely to undervalue the true market value of carriage on cable systems, the FCC's new formula is not unreasonable," said NCTA President Decker Anstrom.
